citation: Kaslow et al. (2018), A model-based systems engineering approach for technical measurement with application to a CubeSat
title: A model-based systems engineering approach for technical measurement with application to a CubeSat
venue_type: Conference paper; venue name not reported in paper text
modeling_scope: System-level CubeSat Reference Model approach for incorporating technical measures into an MBSE model. Scope includes stakeholder concerns, mission objectives, MOE/MOP/TPM specifications and value properties, requirements traceability, mission enterprise architecture, cost and service-life measures, CubeSat power-related MOPs such as battery cycles and solar cell life, propulsion TPM example, constraint blocks, parametric diagrams, trade analysis, risk/technical progress monitoring, and conceptual V&V linkage. It is not an EPS architecture paper and does not model EPS-specific verification procedures.
mbse_language_method_tool: SysML is used, including a technical measures profile, stereotypes/model elements for stakeholder concerns, mission objectives, MOE/MOP/TPM specifications, value properties, constraint blocks, parametric diagrams, trace relationships, and a CubeSat Reference Model. No specific modeling tool is reported.
robot_platform: CubeSat/nanosatellite-class platform; examples are taken from a CubeSat Reference Model. The mission enterprise includes a ground system, launch system, and CubeSat. Specific form factor and named flight mission are not reported.
task_domain: CubeSat systems engineering and technical measurement for assessing mission objectives such as operational lifetime/service life and total mission cost; specific operational payload/domain is not reported.
interface: Model-integration interfaces are trace relationships and parametric bindings among stakeholder concerns, mission objectives, requirements, MOE/MOP/TPM properties, constraints, and architecture elements. Physical spacecraft interfaces are not reported.
feedback: Technical measures are described as tracked and assessed to provide insight, early indications of development issues, prediction of performance-requirement satisfaction, risk monitoring, and evaluation of mitigation actions. Parametric analysis lets different solutions be evaluated against MOEs; no closed-loop simulation is reported.
evaluation: The paper evaluates/demonstrates the approach through worked SysML examples from the CubeSat Reference Model, including mission enterprise MOEs for service life and total cost, CubeSat MOPs for DeltaV, battery cycles, solar cell life, and cost, and propulsion TPMs used in a DeltaV parametric relation. No empirical validation, case deployment result, or quantitative mission-outcome evaluation is reported.
rq_relevance: RQ1 partial: the paper provides a general system-level CubeSat MBSE/reference-model approach using SysML technical measures, but it is not focused on EPS behavior; power appears only through battery-cycle and solar-cell-life MOPs. RQ2 partial: it claims MBSE/modeling outcomes such as traceability, reduced development risk, improved quality, trade analysis, enhanced communications, and generalizability, but does not quantify reliability, reproducibility, or EPS-specific integration outcomes. RQ3 partial: it links MOEs/MOPs/TPMs to validation and verification conceptually, but says future work is needed to incorporate V&V model elements and does not provide EPS-specific verification procedures.
claimed_outcomes: MBSE/model-centric approach is claimed to provide enhanced communications, reduced development risk, improved quality, and enhanced knowledge transfer.
The technical-measures approach is claimed to provide clear traceability from stakeholder concerns to TPMs, allowing impacts of changes to be easily assessed.
Textual MOE/MOP/TPM specifications are claimed to broaden the scope to include qualitative and quantitative technical measures within the system model.
Constraint blocks and parametric diagrams are claimed to support performance analysis, trade analyses, and assessment of different solutions against MOEs.
The approach is claimed to be tool-independent and general enough for incorporation into many systems engineering methodologies.

In the CubeSat context, the paper says technical measurement could play a role in increasing mission success, but it reports no quantified reliability result and no EPS-specific reproducibility or integrability outcome.
verification_validation_linkage: General system-level linkage only. The paper states that MBSE supports verification and validation, that MOEs are used to validate user needs, MOPs verify requirements, and TPMs assess progress toward technical requirements. It also states that technical measures form a basis for V&V, but future work is needed to incorporate V&V model elements and relate them to these measures. No EPS-specific verification/test procedure model is provided.
key_findings: The paper presents a SysML technical-measures profile for stakeholder concerns, mission objectives, MOE/MOP/TPM specifications, and mop/tpm value-property stereotypes.

The proposed flow derives mission objectives from stakeholder concerns, derives MOE specifications from objectives, translates MOEs into mission-enterprise value properties, and traces them back to originating concerns.
For the CubeSat example, service life is modeled as depending on DeltaV, battery cycles, and solar cell life; total cost is modeled as the sum of ground-system, launch-system, and CubeSat costs.
MOPs and TPMs are related to higher-level measures using SysML constraint blocks and parametric diagrams, enabling solution comparison and trade analysis.
The approach is system-level and reference-model oriented; it includes limited power-related measures but no detailed EPS architecture, EPS behavior model, or EPS-specific V&V procedure.
limitations_gaps: The abstract states that little literature ties technical measurement and MBSE together and that existing literature treats the topic generally and without details.
The related-work section states that prior model-based technical-measures applications lack a system model and therefore lack traceability to requirements, structure, behavior, and verification.

The related-work section states that prior SysML technical-measure approaches are incomplete and lack traceability to stakeholder expectations, connections between technical measures, and connections with requirements.
The future-work section states that model elements associated with verification and validation still need to be incorporated and related to the technical measures.
No formal limitations, threats to validity, or empirical evaluation limitations are discussed.

quality.rationale: A DOI and conference-paper format are provided, but the paper text available here does not state the venue name. The paper discusses gaps in prior work and future V&V work, but it does not include a formal limitations or validity discussion.
